Based on the provided context, the original Roman calendar consisted of only ten months. The names of the later months reflected their numerical order in this early system. For example, "September" meant seventh, "October" meant eighth, "November" meant ninth, and **"December"** meant tenth. The text explicitly notes that December was the last month of the original calendar, signifying its position as the tenth month before the addition of January and February and subsequent reforms.
